summary: Today’s PaymentsDive recap: 8 new stories, with focus on product + fintech innovation.

articles.title: FIS, Toast CFOs exit
articles.description: The chief financial officers are leaving the payments players as the companies grapple with separate challenges.

articles.title: Block reaches $964M DOJ pact
articles.description: The company would pay $764 million of the amount in the agreement to resolve U.S. charges that its anti-money laundering program was ineffective.

articles.title: Payments firm settles FTC fees case
articles.description: Riverside Payments and its affiliates agreed to pay $600,000 to resolve allegations they misled small businesses about processing costs.

articles.title: Truist bolsters merchant tools
articles.description: The super-regional rolled out a faster onboarding experience and added insights for business owners, said Chris Ward, head of enterprise payments.

articles.title: Fiserv talks to potential asset buyers
articles.description: The processor has started engaging with potential buyers for the sale of some of its assets, the CEO said. It has also doubled its savings goal to $1 billion.

articles.title: Google makes big plans for wallet
articles.description: The tech giant envisions its digital wallet assuming a larger role in commerce than merely point-of-sale payments, Google’s payments head said.

articles.title: Bilt tackles sports with $300M deal
articles.description: The rent-rewards startup aims to stretch beyond housing payments and credit cards by buying Lava, a technology firm that focuses on sports loyalty.

articles.title: Mastercard scales in India
articles.description: The card network expanded its tie with the country’s largest private bank, increasing its opportunities to sell to small businesses and consumers.
